# Haneul Tower — level design (v2)

**Haneul** means *sky*. A Siege-style 5v5 attack/defend map set on three consecutive upper floors of a
fictional mixed-use supertall in Seoul, 2111: a rainy night near midnight, 403 m above the river.
The building is not the Crystalix tower and has nothing to do with Crystalix. All buildings, brands and
companies are fictional, and no real landmark is reproduced.

**Read this first.** `layout.json` is the single source of truth. It is generated by
`tools/build_layout.py` (the design tables). After any change, run:

```
cd map && python3 tools/build_layout.py && python3 tools/validate_layout.py && python3 tools/render_plans.py layout.json t-design2 && python3 tools/navtime.py
```

- The validator must report **0 errors**. It currently reports 22 warnings: 21 door-chain lines of
  30–40 m (listed, see §7) and Booth 2's single door (intended).
- `render_plans.py [layout] [outdir]` renders the plans (`t-design2/` for this revision; pass the repo's
  `floorplans/` folder for delivery).
- If you hand-edit `layout.json`, port the edit back into the generator or stop using it.
- v2 is a revision after a competitive critique. §11 lists what changed, what was rejected and why.
  The v1 files are kept as `layout.v1.json`, `DESIGN.v1.md` and `tools.v1bak/`.

> **World rule (all assets): no logos and no readable text** in any geometry or texture: no Hangul,
> no Latin, no digits, no pseudo-script. Abstract graphics on screens and holograms are fine. Lift
> indicators and exit signs use pictograms only. Callout names live only in the UI overlay and the
> floor plans.

---

## 1. Concept and identity

**The tower.** A 128-storey softened-square supertall on the north bank of the river, in a dense
fictional business district. Its glass faces have vertical aluminium fins, with a purple (#8a4dff) edge
light on every third fin. Offices fill the lower block and a sky hotel and media company the upper
block. At 96F the tower steps back on the river side, and the roof of the lower block becomes an open
sky terrace. Above the map, 99F is a mechanical floor: a belt-truss band of dark louvres and diagonal
lattice bracing that carries the BMU rail. The tower then continues about 30 floors to a lattice crown
roughly 134 m above the terrace. Below the map there is only the sheer drop to the wet, reflective
streets.

**Mood** (from the reference image, mood only):
- dark glass towers with purple edge-lit facades;
- huge translucent holographic screen walls on neighbouring towers (abstract figures and shapes, never text);
- warm interior light behind glass; rain streaks on every pane, rain sheeting down the Garden's 7.3 m glass;
- elevated glass walkways and skybridges between towers far below;
- the river with long lit bridges and red and white light trails; lightning pulses over the river
  (an emissive sky pulse every 20–40 s, no extra lights);
- dark mountain ridges ringing the city in the rain;
- a generic lattice broadcast tower lit purple and pink on a forested hill to the north-north-east.

**Korean identity without text.** Contemporary Korean design blended with 2111 tech:
- warm wood lattice (*changsal*) on props and screens only (see §8 for the wall language);
- translucent hanji paper panels: the soft walls themselves, hanji ceiling tiles, lantern planters;
- stone and warm ondol floors with glowing seams; dry-stone feature walls;
- a modern pavilion with steep sweeping eaves in the sky garden;
- restrained traditional colour accents (deep indigo, cinnabar red, ochre) on charcoal, stone and wood,
  under the purple neon; celadon vases in the executive floor;
- outside: the river, the bridges, the ridges, the forested hill with the lattice tower.

### The three floors

| Map floor | Tower level | y (floor) | Programme | Signature spaces | Site |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **F1** | 96F *Garden Level* | 0.0 | Sky garden, spa, sky-hotel kitchen and back of house | **Garden** (double height, pavilion, pool, Garden Stair with a stone mid-landing), the sky terrace outside | S4 Tea Room / Ondol Lounge |
| **F2** | 97F *Sky Lobby* | 4.2 | Hotel sky lobby, skybridge arrival, broadcast studio floor, lounge bar | **Gallery** over the garden, **Studio** (double height, holo stage hologram), **Skybridge** | S2 Concierge / Deposit, S3 Lounge Bar / Wine Room |
| **F3** | 98F *Broadcast* | 8.4 | Media floor: control room, render farm, newsroom, executive suite | **Grid** catwalks A/B/C over the stage, **Control Room** director window, Screening room | S1 Control Room / Render Farm |

The ceiling of F3 is the underside of 99F, the mechanical floor: hard, never opened.

**Two diagonal voids.** The **Garden** (SW) is double height from F1 to F2; the **Studio** (NE) from F2 to
F3. Each has an open stair and vertical sightlines.

### What you see from where (for `parts/exterior.js`)

| Facing | View |
| --- | --- |
| South (+z), river | The wide river about 1.2 km across, 4–5 long lit bridges with light trails, a low island park, the south bank towers, and a dark ridge beyond in rain. Seen through the Garden's 7 m glass, the Veranda, the River Lounge and the Suite. The terrace spawn faces the tower's south face. |
| North (−z) | Dense towers stepping up to the forested hill with the lattice broadcast tower about 3 km NNE, the highest ridge behind it. The **Crane Deck** neighbour (under construction) is close to the NW, with its tower crane, site hut, gantry and hoist ramp. |
| East (+x) | **East Tower**, a neighbouring glass tower 30 m away, with a huge translucent holo screen wall on its west face. The **Skybridge** runs to it at F2 and the **Bridge Truss** hangs under it. |
| West (−x) | **West Roof**, the roof of a lower neighbouring tower 1.5 m below F1 and 10 m away, with a plant room, a cooling tower and a lettering-free helipad ring, linked by the **Catwalk** and the **South Catwalk**. |
| Up | The fins and the 99F belt-truss band 4 m above F3, the facade rising into the rain, and the crown far above. |
| Down | 400 m of glass and fins down to wet neon streets; straight down through the Skybridge's glass floor panel. |

## 2. Scale numbers

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Floor plate | chamfered square 52 × 52 m (x, z ∈ [−26, 26]), 5 m chamfers, **2,654 m²** gross per floor |
| Core | 18 × 18 m concrete, x, z ∈ [−9, 9], outer walls 0.6 m, inner 0.3 m (hard) |
| Floor to floor | **4.2 m**: ceiling 3.1 m, plenum 0.8 m, slab 0.3 m (slab spans y−0.3…y) |
| Double-height rooms | 7.3 m clear (Garden on F1, Studio on F2) |
| Perimeter columns | centres 1 m inside the glass: 1.0 m at 0 and ±18 on each face (faces 24.5…25.5), 1.6 m mega columns at ±9 (24.2…25.8), 1.4 m corner columns at (±22.8, ±22.8) |
| Column wraps | a partition that meets the glass on a column line stops at the column face; the strip to the glass is a hard **column wrap** (1.8 m at mega, 1.5 m at perimeter columns); 30 wraps |
| Curtain wall | 3.0 m bays of two 1.5 m lites (chamfer bays 3.536 m), vision 0–3.1 m, spandrel 3.1–4.2 m |
| Doors | single 1.0 × 2.0 m, double 2.0 × 2.0 m (door heads on the 2.0 m transom line) |
| Interior windows | sill 1.0, head 2.0 |
| Facade entry windows | one 1.5 m lite, sill 0.45, head 2.0, tempered transom above; ≥ 1.2 m clear of columns |
| Wall thickness | hard 0.4 (core 0.6 / 0.3), reinforceable 0.2, soft 0.15, interior glass 0.08, balustrade 0.06 (1.1 m high) |
| Reinforcement | units on the clear defender face, ≥ 0.05 m hard trim each end, 0.26 m deployed depth, 0.3 m hard jamb where two reinforceable walls of one room meet; budget **8 per round** |
| Ledges | 0.8 m grating outside the glass at every floor level (F1: W, N, E; the south is the terrace), 1.1 m rail |
| Rappel | anywhere on the facade from y 0 to 12.2 (the BMU rail on the 99F band) |
| Playable area | about 7,300 m² of interior over three floors, plus the terrace (≈2,200 m²) and the approaches |

## 3. Floor plans and callouts

Callout names are the room `name` fields; the plans in `t-design2/plan_F*.png` show them. Areas in m².
**(S)** marks a site room. Names are unique per floor and comms-safe (v1 had three "East Hall"s).

### Core (identical on every floor, all hard)
- **Lifts lobby** x[−9,9] z[−2,2], named per floor: **Garden Lifts** (F1), **Sky Lifts** (F2), **Media Lifts**
  (F3). A 4 m corridor straight through the core, barricadable double doors at both ends (x = ±9).
- **Stair A** (NE quarter; doors to the lobby and the east ring at x = 9, z ≈ −3), **Stair B** (SW quarter;
  doors to the lobby and the west ring at x = −9, z ≈ 3).
- **Shaft** (NW): service lift shaft, pried doors on every floor, ladder F1 to F3.
- Lift banks and risers are solid; their lift doors are closed, hard decoration with pictogram indicators.

## 4. Objective sites

Each site is two adjacent rooms with an objective marker each (`sites[].objectives`) and a defender spawn
inside (`spawns.defenders`). Each site has reinforceable walls on its attack sides, soft walls on its
rotation sides, a hard sightline anchor, and hatches or soft floor patches.

**Reinforcement budget: 8 per defending team per round** (`rules.reinforce.budget`); a wall unit of any
size counts 1, a hatch counts 1. Every site offers 10–12 candidates, so defenders must choose. Units are
Wall Fortification gadgets (XL 4.0, large 3.0, standard 1.5, small 1.0 m wide, all 2.0 m high, hatch
1.2 m). Walls listed as two units leave a soft gap if only one is placed; the unit seams show in the
finish (§8).

| Site | Candidates | Wall units (attack side faced) | Hatches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | 10 | F3_W17 XL, F3_W19 L (Media Hall, Control); F3_W20 L, F3_W22 XL (Media Hall, Render); F3_W16 Std+S (Grid C); F3_W27 L (Edit 1); F3_W29 XL (Edit 2) | H14, H15 in the site floor, from above |
| S2 | 10 | F2_W55 L, F2_W57 L (Studio); F2_W60 XL+S, F2_W61 L+Std (Vault Hall); F2_W67 XL, F2_W69 L (Bridge Lobby) | H07, H08 from below |
| S3 | 10 | F2_W14 L, F2_W16 XL (Gallery); F2_W20 XL, F2_W22 XL, F2_W24 XL+S (Cellar Hall); F2_W28 L, F2_W29 XL (Cigar Room) | H09, H10 from below |
| S4 | 12 | F1_W22 XL+Std, F1_W23 XL (Spa Hall); F1_W25 XL, F1_W27 L, F1_W28 L, F1_W30 L (Veranda); F1_W32 Std (Changing); F1_W34 Std+S (Steam Room) | H01, H02 from below |

### S1 — F3 Control Room / Render Farm (north, top floor)
- **Rooms.** Control Room x[0,9] z[−26,−12]; Render Farm x[−9,0] z[−26,−12]; shared soft wall with a door
  and a barricadable window.
- **Hard anchors.** The Render Farm's west **vault fire wall** (x = −9, z −26…−22.1) and the Control Room's
  **void wall** (x = 9, z −26…−22): this has no attacker footing on the void side, so it is hard.
- **Reinforceable.** Media Hall side of both rooms: Control XL (x 0…4.2) | door | L (x 5.7…9); Render L
  (x −3.2…0) | door | XL (x −9…−4.5, with a 0.3 m jamb at the Render SW corner). Grid C side: Std+S
  (z −15…−12, jamb at the Control SE corner). Render west: L to Edit 1, XL to Edit 2.
- **Glass.** The 5 m director window over the stage: unreinforceable, the site's weak point.
- **Vertical.** Top floor, so vertical play comes from below: hatches **H14** (Control) and **H15** (Render)
  in the site floor, which attackers blow open from the Green Room and Makeup to shoot up (defenders can
  reinforce them face-up); soft patches P01 and P02 cannot be reinforced.
- **Attack.** Crane Deck → gantry → north ledge → north windows or the Edit rooms; bridge roof → F3 east
  ledge → grid window → Grid A → grid door or **Grid C** → Std+S wall / Media Hall; stage → shoot the
  director window, Studio Stair; F2 → H14/H15/P01/P02 from below.
- **Defence.** Director window over the grid; the holo console turns the stage hologram on; Grid C and the
  Media Hall give a second rotation to Stair A that bypasses the core.

### S2 — F2 Concierge / Deposit (east, mid floor)
- **Rooms.** Concierge x[12,26] z[0,9]; Deposit x[12,26] z[−9,0]; shared wall soft with a door (x 12…19) and
  the glass lockbox gallery (x 19…26).
- **Hard anchors.** The Studio's **LED volume backing** (z = −9, x 12…16) and the core behind Vault Hall.
- **Reinforceable.** Studio side L | studio window | L (stopping at the mega-column wrap); Vault Hall side
  XL+S (Deposit) and L+Std (Concierge); Bridge Lobby side XL | double door | L.
- **Vertical.** H07 (Archive → Deposit) and H08 (Writers Room → Concierge), reinforced from below; soft patch
  P05 in the Concierge floor (shoot up from Lockers). v1's second Archive → Deposit opening (P03) moved to
  the Screening room.
- **Attack.** Skybridge → portal → round the bridge screen → Bridge Lobby side; Studio floor → Deposit north;
  bridge roof → F3 Archive and Writers Room → hatches; Lockers → P05.
- **Defence.** Vault Hall is the rotation spine; studio window and lockbox glass give internal lines; roam
  the Studio, the grid and the Bridge Lobby.

### S3 — F2 Lounge Bar / Wine Room (west, mid floor)
- **Rooms.** Lounge Bar x[−26,−12] z[0,9]; Wine Room x[−20,−12] z[−12,0]; glass wine wall with a double door.
  The Cigar Room x[−26,−20] z[−12,0] is the attackers' foothold.
- **Hard anchors.** The **stone cellar wall** (z = −12, x −20…−12) and the core behind Cellar Hall.
- **Reinforceable.** Gallery side: column wrap | L | **XL facing the Garden Stair head** | double door | bar
  glass (x −14.7…−12). Cellar Hall side: XL (Lounge), XL and XL+S (Wine). Cigar side: L (Lounge north) and XL
  (Wine west).
- **Glass.** The bar glass now sits east of the stair head: it sees across the stair head, and the stair
  flight only through the tempered balustrade (see, not shoot).
- **Vertical.** H09 (Newsroom → Lounge Bar) and H10 (Podcast → Wine Room, dressed as the wine lift),
  reinforced from below; soft patches P04 (from the Newsroom) and P06 (Lounge Bar floor, shoot up from the
  Canteen).
- **Attack.** West Roof → Catwalk → Staff Entry → Service Hall → Stair B → Cellar Hall; West Ladder → F2 ledge
  → Cigar Room window; terrace → Garden Doors → Garden Stair → Gallery; Hoist Ramp → Noraebang → Cellar Hall;
  F3 → hatches.
- **Defence.** Gallery rail and bar glass over the garden; reinforce Cellar Hall; roam the Noraebang, the
  Booths and the Gallery.

### S4 — F1 Tea Room / Ondol Lounge (south, bottom floor)
- **Rooms.** Tea Room x[−9,0] z[12,21] (raised maru platform, lattice screen); Ondol Lounge x[0,9] z[12,21]
  (warm stone bench); shared hanji wall with a door at z 19.3.
- **Hard anchor.** The **garden stone wall** (x = −9, z 12…21) with one door (z 13.4) into the Garden.
- **Reinforceable.** Veranda side XL | door | L, L | double door | L; Spa Hall side XL+Std (Tea) and XL
  (Ondol); east: Std to Changing, Std+S to the Steam Room (jamb at the Ondol SE corner).
- **Vertical.** H01 and H02 (Reception → site), reinforced from below; **P08**, an unreinforceable soft patch
  in the Reception floor over the Tea Room; H03 and P07 open the River Lounge onto the Veranda.
- **Exterior.** None directly; the Veranda is the buffer, with two entry windows.
- **Attack.** Terrace → Veranda windows → south walls; Garden Doors → Garden → stone door or Garden Lobby →
  Spa Hall; Bath Door or the Bridge Truss window → Bathhouse → Changing / Steam Room → east walls; South
  Catwalk → Garden window; any spawn → Reception → H01/H02/P08.
- **Defence.** Spa Hall and the Garden Lobby are the rotation lane; the Bathhouse and the Garden arcade are
  roam flanks.

### Attackers (all outside the building; each spawn has two landings)

| ID | Name | Level | Spawn cover (no peeks) | Landing 1 (s) | Landing 2 (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A1** | Sky Terrace | F1 (y 0) | points x −2.5…2.5, z 53…55 behind the hard lift kiosk (x −5…5) under the timber canopy (x −6…6, z 52…57) | Garden Doors 7.7, Bath Door 7.8 | Veranda windows 8.6; SE/SW ladders to the F2/F3 ledges |
| **A2** | West Roof | F1 (y −1.5) | points x −64…−66, z −19…−15 in the west lee of the plant room | **Catwalk** (z −5.25, 10 m) → catwalk door 9.7 | **South Catwalk** (z 15.75, 10 m) → Garden entry window 12.7; West Ladder to the F2/F3 ledges |
| **A3** | Skybridge | F2 (y 4.2) | points off the tube axis (z 4…9 and 18…22) behind a hard baffle across the bridge mouth (x 57.5, z 11…16); the hall's west wall is solid except the mouth | Skybridge → portal 8.8 (side doors to the F2 ledge; Bridge Roof Ladder to the F3 east ledge) | service stair → **Bridge Truss** (y 0, under the bridge) → Bathhouse entry window 11.6 |
| **A4** | Crane Deck | F3 (y 8.4) | points inside a roofed site hut (x −50…−42, z −57…−49, walls on its east and south sides) | **Gantry** → gantry door (NW chamfer lite 1) 7.3 | **Hoist Ramp** (ramp-stair down to y 4.2) → Noraebang entry window on the F2 north ledge 12.5 |

- The gantry, both catwalks, the truss and the hoist ramp have solid 1.2 m lower hoarding panels.
- **Spawn-peek check** (`tools/spawn_los.py`, run by the validator): a defender eye 1.6 m up (5.0 m in
  double-height bays), 0.4 m inside every breakable lite, entry window, facade door, the Garden Doors and
  the portal, against attacker eyes 1.0 and 1.7 m above every spawn point. Kiosk, canopy, terrace
  planters, plant room, cooling tower, hut, stacks, mast, the neighbour masses, the East Tower (open only
  through the bridge mouth) and the baffle block; the skybridge's tempered tube is see-through but not
  shoot-through. Result: **0 visible spawn points** (v1: 285 sightline hits).
- **Defender reveal zones** (`exterior.defender_reveal_zones`, nodes `ZONE_EXT_*`): the terrace, every
  ledge, the catwalks, gantry, truss, hoist ramp, skybridge and its roof, the cradle, the West Roof, the
  Crane Deck and the bridge hall. A defender inside one is revealed (runout rule).

### Defenders
A defender spawn sits inside each site pair: **D1** (S1), **D2** (S2), **D3** (S3), **D4** (S4), five points each.

| Bridge Roof Ladder | F2 → bridge roof → F3 ledge | exterior | East Tower end of the bridge |

### Rotations (defenders)
- **The lifts lobby** joins the west and east halls on every floor in under 5 s; also the riskiest line.
- **Stair A and Stair B** link S2 and S3 to the floors above and below.
- **F1** is a full ring: Spa Hall, Garden Lobby, Service Hall, Kitchen Pass, Locker Hall. The Garden Lobby
  means S3/core → S4 no longer crosses the attackers' Garden.
- **F3**: Grid C gives S1 a second link to Stair A (Media Hall → Grid C → Archive Hall) that bypasses the core.

Nav-grid rotation times (objective A to objective A, interior only, `tools/navtime.py`):

|  | S1 | S2 | S3 | S4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | – | 11 s | 12 s | 16 s |
| S2 | 15 s | – | 10 s | 10 s |
| S3 | 15 s | 10 s | – | 7 s |
| S4 | 20 s | 17 s | 10 s | – |

Asymmetric because hatches only work downward.

### Flanks and roam areas
- **Roam:** F1 Garden, Dining Room, Kitchen, Laundry, Bathhouse; F2 Studio, Noraebang and Booths, Reception
  and River Lounge, Gallery, Bridge Lobby; F3 Newsroom, Edit Bay, Screening, Boardroom, the Grid.
- **Flanks:** the Shaft ladder, the Spiral Stair, the Suite Stair, ledges and rappel, the bridge side doors,
  the cradle, Grid C, and each spawn's second landing.
- **Dead zones now have jobs:** F1 north (Dining, Kitchen, Laundry) has H04, H05 and P09 (Studio floor →
  Laundry) above it, and the Cold Store is locked; F3 south has P03 (Screening → Bridge Lobby), H11 and the
  Suite Stair.

| A1 Sky Terrace | 28 | 28 | 17 | 19 | 14 | 19 | **11** | **11** | 7.6 |
| A2 West Roof | 26 | 24 | 28 | 27 | 17 | **16** | 18 | 21 | 9.5 |

Every spawn has a home site 11–16 s away and reaches every site within 28.4 s. First entries are

## 7. Key sightlines and counters

| Sightline | From → to | Counter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lifts lobby | 24 m E–W through the core, every floor | barricadable double doors at both ends; the facing hall walls are reinforceable on F2 |
| Bridge tube | 30 m from the East Tower to the portal | hard bridge screen in the lobby; hall baffle; side doors, bridge roof and truss as alternatives |
| Director window | Control Room → stage floor | shoot it out from the stage, smoke or hologram the stage, climb the Studio Stair, Grid C |
| Grid A / Grid C | catwalks over the stage / along the Control Room void wall | exposed from the stage and the director window |
| Gallery drop | F2 Gallery rail → Garden Doors and floor | pavilion platform, rocks, the arcade, the stone screen |
| Bar glass | Lounge Bar → across the stair head | the stair flight is behind tempered balustrade; stair-head planter; mid-landing |
| Veranda | split by the stone lantern into two 8 m halves | the site's south walls and the Veranda door panels |
| Spa Hall | 23 m behind S4 | the Bathhouse shower block ends it; Garden Lobby door is offset |
| North ledge | gantry landing → Control Room glass | tempered at the landing; breakable lites near S1 let defenders punish ledge walkers |
| Vault Hall | 18 m behind S2 | Studio and Security double doors; camera crane stops the Studio continuation |

**Door chains.** `tools/door_lines.py` (run by the validator) opens every door and window, treats interior
glass and rails as see-through, and looks for lane-wide straight lines (still clear when shifted ±0.25 m)
that pass two or more wall openings. Over 40 m is an error; 30–40 m is a warning. v1 had chains of
45–53 m (including the critique's four: x ≈ −10.5 on F1, F2 and F3, and the F2 Lounge Bar → VIP diagonal).
v2 has none over 40 m and **21 of 30–40 m**, all through at least two barricadable doors; the validator
prints them. Builders must keep the props marked "breaks the … line" exactly where they are.

### Construction rules the builders must follow
- **Visual language (one per type, learnable at a glance).**
  - Soft (by programme): hanji changsal (tti-sal lattice, low backlight) in hotel and spa rooms, dark acoustic
    fabric on the media floor, painted gypsum in back of house. Always thin, with dark studs at the returns.
  - Reinforceable: the same hanji panel below 2.0 m with the **unit seams visible** (thin dark joints at
    every `panels[].u0/u1`), a dark steel transom at 2.0 m, a dark bronze bulkhead above, and steel trims
    at the ends.
  - Hard: one family everywhere: dark honed granite panels (1.2 × 0.6 m, deep reveals) on the core, wraps,
    vault and void walls, or dry stone (garden, cellar, backdrop). Never timber on a hard wall.
  - Wood lattice only on props and free-standing screens, never on walls.
  - Facade tell: tempered lites have a dark dot-frit border (no text); breakable lites are frameless with a
    thin purple edge glow; entry windows are breakable lites with a steel latch sill.
- **Reinforceable bay.**
  - The units sit on the clear defender face: `reinforce.clear` is the free run along the wall (after
    columns, perpendicular walls and jambs); the units are centred in it (`reinforce.panels`, u from wall end
    `a`) with at least 0.05 m of hard trim at each end (`reinforce.trim`). The trims, transom (2.0 m) and
    bulkhead to the slab underside (3.9) are hard.
  - Unit placement: origin = the point at u = (u0+u1)/2 on the wall line, pushed `thickness/2` along
    `defender_side`, at floor level; the unit faces the defender room; `far_side.z = reinforce.far_side_z`
    (−0.2).
  - `defender_side` is `pos` (the room on `+n`) or `neg`. Deployed units are 0.26 m deep; no two deployed
    units, props, columns or walls overlap (validated).
- **Column wraps.** `walls[].column_wrap = <column id>`: a hard casing from the column face to the glass,
  built into the column.
- **Plenum closed.** Every hard, soft and reinforceable wall stores `y1 = 3.9` and rises to the underside of
  the slab above (the 3.1 m ceiling hangs between them); interior glass stops at 3.1 m with a soft drywall
  bulkhead (`SOFT_<id>_bulk`) above. `to_slab: true` is kept on the Studio walls as a marker.
- **Hatch.** A framed 1.2 m square in the slab with a hanji ceiling tile below. `reinforce_from` and
  `mount` say how the gadget goes on: every hatch is `above` = as shipped, face-up on the slab (`mount.up`
  +Y, anchors 0.3 m down), as in Siege. Round 1 had six hatches mounted face-down under the slab; that put the
  unit 3.9 m over the defender, above the ceiling, and broke the terminal eject, so they were moved on top. S2,
  S3 and S4 ceiling hatches are reinforced by a defender in the room above (it counts as that site's
  candidate); S1's H14/H15 are in the site floor.
- **Facade lites.** Each bay has two lites (`lites[].type`). Entry windows and doors carry an `opening`
  with y0/y1; above is a tempered transom, below a hard kick panel. Every entry is ≥ 1.2 m clear of
  columns. Bays with `omit_mullion: true` (Garden Doors F1_S11, portal F2_E11) have no centre mullion or
  fin. The grid window (F2_E01 lite 1) sits at F3 level (y 4.65–6.2 above F2), in line with Grid A.
- **Double-height bays** (`double_height: true`) have vision glass 0–7.3 m and a spandrel at 7.3–8.4 m; the
  floor above has no bay there.
- **Pavilion roof** (`props[].roof`): steep (40°), slide-off collider, eaves at 3.6 m and 1.0 m clear of the
  Gallery edge, so nobody can stand on it.

## 9. Props and cover (`props`)

**88 gameplay props** (v1: 38) the floor builders must place with these footprints and heights. Other
dressing is free, but it must not block doors, entries, hatches, stairs or sightlines more than these do.

- `h` is the top height above the floor; the hot pool is −0.6 (sunken). `cover`: `half` or `full`.
  `type`: `hard` (indestructible) or `soft` (destructible). The holo stage is `shape: round`.
- New props cover every room the critique listed (Bridge Lobby, Cigar Room, Gallery, Lockers, Canteen,
  Plant Room, Staff Entry, Green Room, Makeup, Wardrobe, Podcast, Suite Lounge, Exec Office, Edit 1/2,
  Foyer, Projection, Changing, Steam Room, Veranda, VIP Lounge, Cloakroom); Security keeps its scanner gates.
- The props that break long lines say so in their note (stone screen, shower block, Veranda lantern,
  wine display, staggered Gallery planters, River Lounge planter, arch planters, back bar, wine tower,
  screen totem, camera crane, flight cases, edit rack, vase plinth, news wall). Keep them.
- Validated clearances: 1.0 m in front of every interior opening, 1.5 m inside every facade entry, 1.5 m at
  both ends of every straight stair, and clear of hatches, patches, columns, walls and deployed units.
- The terrace has five more hard planters and a stone lantern wall (h 1.0–1.2) to break the 27 m crossing.
- `cover` (19 entries) lists deployable-shield spots with a facing yaw: hints for the overlay, not geometry.

### Set piece: the stage hologram (`set_pieces`, prefix `HOLO_`)
A 6.4 m abstract hologram (figures and shapes, no text) over the holo stage, r 3.3 m. It **blocks vision,
not bullets**. Defenders switch it on and off at the holo console in the Control Room; attackers kill it for
the round by shooting the emitter ring at the stage rim. It ties S1 and S2 fights to the Studio.

## 10. Contract

### Conventions
- **Units and axes.** Metres. Plan coordinates `[x, z]`, x east, z south (north = −z); y up.
- **Heights.** F1 floor is y = 0; floors at y 0, 4.2, 8.4. Wall and opening `y0`/`y1` are relative to the
  wall's floor. Every `[x, y, z]` point (spawns, objectives, stairs, routes, sightlines, hatch mounts) is
  absolute.
- **Wall normal.** `n = (−dz, dx)/len` for the wall direction a→b. `side_pos` is the room on `+n`,
  `side_neg` the room on `−n`. All interior walls are axis aligned.
- **Outline order.** Clockwise in plan view (N face west→east, then NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW). The inward
  normal of a facade segment uses the same formula.
- **Ids.** Rooms `<floor>_<slug>` (`F2_concierge`); walls `F2_W55`; openings `F2_O31`; bays `F2_E11` (face +
  index along the face); hatches `H01`…, patches `P01`…, props `PR01`…, cover `CV01`…, pilasters `PL01`…
  Ids are stable within a version; v2 renumbered walls, openings and props (builders had not started).

### `layout.json` schema (exact field names)

```

rules           {floor_to_floor, ceiling, slab, plenum, door{w,h}, double_door{w,h}, interior_window{sill,head},
                 facade_entry_window{sill,head},
                 reinforce{height 2.0, header, sizes{xl,large,standard,small}, hatch 1.2, gadget, far_side,
                           budget 8, budget_rule, band 0.26, trim 0.05, pilaster 0.3, placement},
                 thickness{<type>: m}, core_thickness{outer,inner}, curtain_wall{bay, lites_per_bay, chamfer_bay, vision[], spandrel[]},
                 shutters{plane[s0,s1], guide, guide_s[], housing[s0,s1,h], slat, overlap, rail, travel_s, seal, free_end, default, rule, door_lites[], exempt[] {bay, reason}, barricade_clear}}
surface_types   {<type>: {destructible, reinforceable, node_prefix, desc}}   types: hard soft reinforceable glass balustrade
                 open hatch soft_floor door_barricadable window_barricadable opening glass_breakable glass_tempered
                 spandrel portal pilaster glass_floor holo zone_ext shutter

                                  opening? {y0, y1, barricadable}},

```

### Export node naming (glTF; glTFast negates X on import)
Every gameplay node name starts with its surface prefix, so Unity can classify nodes without extras. Every
node also carries glTF `extras`: `{ "surface": "<type>", "id": "<layout id>", "floor": "F2", ...type fields... }`
(`reinforce`, `barricadable`, `rooms`, `reinforce_from` and so on).

| Prefix | Node |
| --- | --- |
| `HARD_` | hard walls `HARD_<wallId>` (column wraps too), reinforce trims/headers `HARD_<wallId>_hdr`, pilasters `HARD_<PLid>`, core `HARD_core_<F>`, columns `HARD_<colId>`, slabs `HARD_slab_<F>`, spandrels `HARD_<bayId>_<lite>`, portal frame `HARD_<bayId>_portal`, hard props `HARD_<propId>` |
| `SOFT_` | soft walls `SOFT_<wallId>` (and soft props `SOFT_<propId>`) |
| `REINF_` | one node per Wall Fortification unit, `REINF_<wallId>_<k>` (k = index in `reinforce.panels`); node origin = unit origin, +Z faces the defender room; extras {size, width, gadget, far_side_z, ...}. The export table in `maps/haneul-tower/INTEGRATION.md` is authoritative. |
| `GLASSI_` | interior glass `GLASSI_<wallId>` |
| `RAIL_` | balustrades and walkway rails |
| `HATCH_` / `SOFTFLOOR_` | `HATCH_<id>` (extras.reinforce_from, extras.mount) and `SOFTFLOOR_<id>`; the matching ceiling piece is `SOFTCEIL_<id>` |
| `BARR_D_` / `BARR_W_` | barricade slot at a barricadable door or window: an empty node at the opening centre, floor level, facing `+n`; extras {w, h, y0, y1, wall, kind} |
| `OPEN_` | non-barricadable opening markers |
| `GLASS_T_` / `GLASS_B_` / `GLASS_TF_` | facade lites `GLASS_T_<bayId>_<k>` / `GLASS_B_<bayId>_<k>`; entry windows are `GLASS_B_` plus a `BARR_W_<bayId>_<k>` slot; the skybridge glass floor `GLASS_TF_skybridge` |
| `HOLO_` | the stage hologram volume `HOLO_stage` (vision blocker, no bullet collider) and its emitter ring `HOLO_stage_emitter` (destructible) |
| `SHUTTER_` | blast shutter `SHUTTER_<bayId>`: base mesh open, one morph target `closed`; clips `shutters_close` / `shutters_open`; its closed-state collider is the box `COL_SHUTTER_<bayId>` (on only while closed); guides and housings are `HARD_shutters_<floor>` |
| `ZONE_EXT_` | defender reveal trigger volumes, one per `defender_reveal_zones` entry (no render geometry) |
| `STAIR_` / `LADDER_` / `WALK_` / `LEDGE_` / `BRIDGE_` / `TERRACE` | circulation; ledges, bridges, truss, ramp and the cradle (`BRIDGE_CR_cradle`, animated) are floors with rails |
| `SPAWN_ATK_<A>_<n>` / `SPAWN_DEF_<D>_<n>` / `OBJ_<id>` / `COVER_<id>` / `CALLOUT_<roomId>` | empty marker nodes (callout extras.name holds the name; never render it in the world) |
| `DECO_` / `ENV_` | dressing and backdrop: no gameplay meaning, may be merged per material |

Keep one node per gameplay surface; never merge across types. Static decoration may be merged per material.

### Tools in `tools/`
- `build_layout.py [-v]`: design tables → `layout.json`; clips walls at columns (column wraps), finds each
  reinforceable wall's clear face and places its units (`-v` prints the fit report).
- `validate_layout.py [layout]`: rooms tile each plate with no overlaps; room edges closed; wall ends attach
  (to walls, facade, core, voids or columns); no crossings or overlaps; no wall runs into a column;
  openings inside their walls and clear of columns; reinforce units on the clear face with trims, no clashes
  with walls, columns, jambs, props or other deployed units; budget candidates per site ≥ budget + 2;
  `reinforce_from` set on every hatch; facade entries ≥ 1.2 m clear of columns and `omit_mullion` where a
  double door crosses the centre mullion; prop clearances at openings, facade entries and stair ends;
  connectivity; hatches and patches clear of walls, voids and props; objectives, spawns and cover in the
  right rooms; spawn peeks (`spawn_los.py`, must be 0); door chains (`door_lines.py`, > 40 m error, 30–40 m
  warning); site wall mix and vertical play; surface counts.
- `render_plans.py [layout] [outdir]`: one plan per floor (walls by type, unit ticks and hard trims,
  defender-side dots, jambs, callouts, sites, spawns, hatches with their reinforce side, stairs, ladders,
  props, cover, lites, ledges, approaches, hologram) and an overview (site plan, routes, timings, mini plans).
- `navtime.py [layout] [--json out]`: nav-grid timings (now with both catwalks, the truss, the hoist ramp
  and the cradle) and reachability.
- `spawn_los.py`, `door_lines.py`, `facade_clear.py`: the checks above, also runnable alone;
  `chain_rooms.py`: debug helper listing the rooms each long chain crosses.

## 11. Revision 2: critique applied

### Accepted
- **P0-1 columns.** Walls meeting the glass on a column line now stop at the column face; the strip to the
  glass is a hard column wrap (30). The validator checks walls and openings against columns. Re-cuts: F2
  Deposit north L | window | L ending at the C_E−9 wrap; Concierge south XL | double door | L ending at the
  C_E+9 wrap; Lounge Bar south starts at the C_W+9 wrap.
- **P0-2 clear face.** Units are sized and placed on the clear defender face with ≥ 0.05 m hard trims,
  computed by the generator and re-checked by the validator, including a 0.26 m deployed-depth clash test.
  The two inside corners got 0.3 m hard jambs (PL03 Render SW, PL01 Ondol SE), and so did the new Control
  SE corner (PL02).
  Implemented as flush jambs in the yielding wall rather than a box in the room, which would clash with the
  other wall's units.
- **P0-3 S1 footing.** The Control Room void wall (z −26…−22) is hard; the Media Hall side is XL | door | L;

### Changed from the critique's numbers
- **Column wrap widths** are 1.8 m (mega) and 1.5 m (perimeter): the perimeter columns face at 24.5, not 24.7.
- **Re-cut coordinates** carry the 0.05 m trims, so they differ by 0.1–0.2 m from the critique's (for
  example Deposit north L x 16…19.1 | window x 19.1…21.1 | L x 21.1…24.2).
- **The A3 spawn hall** grew to x 56…66, z 3…24 so the off-axis points fit inside it.
- **West Roof and Crane hut moved closer.** Adopting the critique's A2/A4 points made A2 the slowest spawn
  (11 s to the building). The West Roof now sits 10 m from the tower (catwalks 10 m, not 18 m) with the
  plant room and points shifted with it, and the A4 hut sits nearer the gantry head. The peek check still
  reports 0.
- **A4's second landing** is a hoist ramp to the F2 north ledge (at x −11.25), not a moving hoist cage: there is
  already one moving platform (the cradle), and a static ramp is easier to read and to build.

### Rejected
- **Veranda glass floor (P3-19).** Below the Veranda is 95F interior, not a drop, so a glass floor would show
  an office ceiling. The glass floor went only into the Skybridge.
- **Door chains under 30 m everywhere.** A 52 m plate cannot avoid every 30–40 m line through two broken doors
  without walling up rooms. v2 makes over 40 m an error and lists the 21 lines of 30–40 m as warnings; all of
  them need at least two barricades broken first.

## Game rule from the user (overrides anything above)

**Every destructible wall can be reinforced.** There is no "soft but unreinforceable" wall: every soft
wall segment is also reinforceable (split into Wall Fortification-sized panels with hard trims), and the
overlay, floor plans, layout.json (`reinforceable: true`), glb extras and HaneulTowerMap.cs must agree.
Hatches stay reinforceable. Hard walls, glass and barricadable openings are unchanged.

## 12. Review round 1 fixes (art and tech)

- **Stairs walkable in Unity:** `COL_STAIR_*_landing` / `_mid` plates on every core-stair floor and mid landing and
  on the Garden Stair landing; the Spiral Stair has one `COL_STAIR_ST_spiral_<k>` box per tread (the mid-height
  plate is gone). Rafters are clipped 0.3 m clear of stairwells and slab openings (a clipping bug also drew one
  rafter 28 m long across the core).
- **Plenum closed:** see the construction rules (walls to 3.9 m, glass bulkheads).
- **Hatches:** all reinforced from above (above).
- **Clearances:** the Garden Stair foot moved 0.8 m north (z 23.8) to clear the SW door; the screens over F2_O16
  and F2_O33/O35 were raised to a 2.22–2.25 m lower edge; the studio truss lowered its cans to 2.34 m over the
  grid catwalks.
- **Lighting:** tube strips only in back of house; other rooms get recessed downlights with soft light-pool decals
  (`pool_*` materials, exported) and story lighting: dim purple Control Room with blue screen spill, blue cold
  aisles in the Render Farm, a dark stone wine wall with warm niche lamps, the Tea Room lit by its hanji
  lightbox. Dark rooms (`DARKROOM` in core.js) have no downlights. Hanji glow and bloom were cut.
- **Room identity:** director's sill console (Control), LED rack bay in the fire wall (Render), two lockbox walls
  (Deposit), backlit onyx (Concierge), bronze bar raft (Lounge Bar), wine niches (Wine Room), timber ceilings in
  the hotel rooms; built-ins only, no furniture.
- **Sky garden:** basalt-edged moss beds with pines and maples, stepping stones, uplight lines, a basalt pool rim,
  a darker low-contrast tile roof on the pavilion with exposed warm rafters and cinnabar ends.
- **Exterior:** fewer, warmer lit windows in the city; a soft volumetric holo figure with ribbon and glow parallax
  layers; rain haze rings, ridge rim light, a rounded forested hill; soft wet patches instead of puddle decals;
  denser, thinner rain; dark wet skybridge and crane decks, a lit site hut, corten planters, a dark timber canopy.
- **Viewer:** furniture footprints show only with the markers (M or P). New hero/preview camera over the river.

**Fewer destructible walls (user, overrides anything above).** Every corner and T-junction of walls is
non-destructible: each wall arm meeting a corner or T is hard for at least 1.0 m from the junction. A
breakable panel only exists in the straight run between two hard ends; a run with less than 2.4 m left between
its hard ends becomes fully hard. Breakable walls are then all reinforceable (rule above). Aim for clearly
fewer breakable walls overall, keeping the important ones per site (attack walls, rotation holes).

*Applied (tools/build_layout.py, junction pass):* junctions are found from wall geometry (an end on another wall or on
the facade; a wall stopped by a perimeter column counts from the glass, so the column wrap is its hard end); door,
window and vault jambs are 0.15 m hard; walls with no run left are hard (`hardened` in layout.json); runs are filled
with the widest flush row of units (`fill_panels`). Before: 140 breakable walls (112 soft + 28 reinforceable), 679 m.
After: 72 reinforceable walls, 169 units, 337.5 m. Site tweaks to keep attack walls: S1 Media Hall doors moved next to
the centre and west junctions (Control door x 1.6, Render door x -7.6), render fire wall ends at z -22.6; S4 Ondol
veranda double door moved to x 7.4 and the Ondol/Changing door to z 13.4. Candidates per site: S1 11, S2 12, S3 10, S4 14
(budget 8). The validator checks the 1.0 m rule independently and rejects any soft wall.

**Backdrop as one mesh (user, overrides anything above).** The whole city skyline backdrop (all BACKDROP /
neighbour scenery that is not gameplay geometry) is merged into ONE mesh with ONE material (bake/atlas its
textures and window emissive into one texture set), in the viewer glb and the Unity copy. No 2 km tiles.
Gameplay neighbours (spawn roofs, crane, skybridge, anything with colliders or typed nodes) stay separate.

*Applied (core.js `buildBackdrop`, parts/exterior.js):* every `skyline` piece is baked into `BACKDROP_city`, one mesh
(132k triangles; the sky dome is another 4.6k) with one material `backdrop_city` (baseColor and emissive atlases 4096², metallic-roughness 2048²),
always one draw call, in both glbs; the Unity copy has no tiles. The sky dome carries the baked cloud deck as
`BACKDROP_sky`. To get there without alpha or blending: the far city bands are building silhouettes in geometry, the
river sheen and light streaks are painted into one opaque water strip cut out of the water sheet, the holo screens
are opaque emissive, ridge crests stay under the cloud deck, and the mist, rain haze rings and hill halo are
viewer-only. The `ENV_NB_*` neighbour bodies and Haneul's own `ENV_` parts stay separate (seen at arm's length).

**Blast shutters on every outer room (user, overrides anything above).** *"Can you have some blastdoors on each outer
room so people spawning outside can't just see through all windows? Keep the doors open for now though."* Every facade
bay with glass gets a heavy armoured shutter that, closed, blocks sight and bullets over the whole bay. They are open by
default and stay open for now.

*Applied (tools/build_layout.py `shutters`, core.js `buildShutters`, validate_layout.py, render_plans.py, the viewer,
HaneulTowerMap.cs):*
- **166 shutters** (F1 58, F2 55, F3 53): every bay with glass, entry windows included, none on a bay with a door (see the
  next note); the two opaque Cold Store bays (F1_N04, F1_N05, all spandrel) have none. The skybridge tube needs none, since
  the portal is its only way in. Double-height Garden and Studio bays get one 7.3 m shutter.
- **Inside the glass, housed in the plenum.** The curtain runs 0.30–0.37 m inside the glass, behind the mullions, door
  frames and barricade slots, so the facade, ledges, fins, reveal zones and rappel are untouched. Open, the slats stack
  in a housing above the ceiling that fills the plenum to the slab; the room shows only slim dark guide channels on the
  mullion lines with one small purple status dot each. Outside it would have cut across the ledges and the rappel line
  and spoiled the facade.
- **No peek gaps.** Closed, a shutter covers the floor to the bay's vision top and runs into its housing. Each end
  either sits in a guide channel that meets the next bay's guide (on any floor), or runs 4 cm into a column or a hard
  wall end. Interior glass (it breaks) and balustrades (1.1 m) never count as a seal. The validator re-checks every bay.
- **Motion:** 0.25 m slats that overlap 3 cm, each moving straight down, so the curtain stays closed at every point of
  its 2.0 s travel. In the glb, the base mesh is open and the morph target `closed` drops it; clips `shutters_close` /
  `shutters_open`. In the viewer, the **Shutters** button or B. In Unity, `HaneulTowerMap.SetShutters` (all, or per
  floor, room or site), with events; the `COL_SHUTTER_` box collides only while the shutter is closed.
- **Dressing kept clear:** facade ceiling coves sit 0.64 m inside the glass, wall panelling and rafters stop 0.46 m from
  it, and the laundry duct, the salt-brick ceiling, one garden bed, the Grid steel, the Exec Hall ceiling slats and its warm wall light line,
  the Garden mist sheets (their SW corners) and the screening tiers (PR73, now x ≤ 24.2) were trimmed. A facade barricade must stay within 0.16 m of its slot.

**No shutter for the door (user, overrides the shutter note above).** *"also, dont have a shutter for the door"*.
Door openings are exempt from the blast shutters; windows and entry windows keep theirs.

*Applied (tools/build_layout.py, validate_layout.py, core.js `buildShutters`, docs):*
- **Garden Doors (F1_S11) and the skybridge portal (F2_E11): no shutter.** The Garden double door spans the bay middle

- **The four facade doors keep a narrower shutter over the glass lite only:** F1_SE00 Bath Door, F1_SW00 Garden side

- **Lone guides:** a guide whose mullion line has no shutter on the other side (the door side, or the neighbour of a

- **Validator:** door bays must have no shutter, no curtain or guide may reach into a door lite, every glass lite must
